# Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: Ramanujan and Arthur weight constraints

Part II of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands: weight-theoretic constraints on the parent’s global parameters. It plans the generic Ramanujan theorem in the central-compact sector, with a fixed-ι tempered anchor or an arithmetic discrete-series anchor; propagation of complementary series and elimination of extraneous points; and the required local-parameter, globalization and cohomological inputs. The partial layers name their missing supplier contracts. The Arthur endpoint concerns weight patterns and normalized real Satake parts, while a global Arthur homomorphism and the discrete decomposition remain conjectural. The local classification and nilpotent-orbit theory are imported from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroupsPartII and LieHighestWeightPartII. The complete targets, hypotheses, proof routes, API and tests are in the companion reader. Layers RA.0–RA.8 have the scope described below; only RA.1 is currently marked planned. The other directions in the original brief remain separate roadmaps.

stages.title: Geometric local parameters and pure Weil–Deligne parameters
stages.description: **Targets.** Integer-weight geometric L-homomorphisms with finite inertia (Ciubotaru–Harris §2.3, Definition 2.5, p.7), and independence of a faithful realization using tensor generation. Distinguish arithmetic Weil–Deligne purity from fixed-ι purity and boundedness. State the weight–monodromy convention with N lowering weights by 2. Pure completion is unique in the fixed-ι GL_n case; the general reductive assertion uses adjoint boundedness and derived-centralizer conjugacy (Gan–Harris–Sawin Lemma 3.5, p.9), not common-weight purity in every faithful representation. The RD.6 tensor-generator converse is requested.

stages.title: Weights of ℓ-adic local systems on curves
stages.description: **Targets.** Lafforgue’s constant-field twist decomposition (Corollaire VII.8, pp.201–202) and geometricity propagation from one boundary place (Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 2.7, pp.7–8). Sawin–Templier’s real-weight filtration and purity for parameters in no proper parabolic (Lemma 11.4, p.83) give common weights in irreducible algebraic realizations. For semisimple G the resulting arithmetic weight is 0; reductive centres require a separate normalization. Import the curve weight theory from DWP.5/DWP.8 and GS.6.

stages.title: Rational Satake classes of cuspidal parameters
stages.description: **Targets.** The relation between a cuspidal representation π and a parent excursion parameter σ, its associated local systems L(π,τ), rationality of Satake classes (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 3.6, p.10), and normalized real parts satisfying 2⟨μ,ν_w⟩=weight(μ). The nonsplit coefficient/support extension of FA.6 is requested; it is not supplied by the existing split integral-model target.

stages.title: Local semisimple parameters and geometric representations
stages.description: **Targets.** Framed local-to-global shtuka uniformization and Li-Huerta’s comparison of Genestier–Lafforgue and Fargues–Scholze parameters (Theorems A/C and §§5–6). Plan geometric representations and stability under coefficient transport, normalized induction, Jacquet modules, products and geometric twists (Ciubotaru–Harris Proposition 3.10, pp.10–11), with finite-length Hecke descent. For nonsplit tori use componentwise residue cardinalities, not a uniformizer criterion with an incorrect residue-degree normalization. Restrict central characters to the smooth central torus. Request the equal-characteristic HS2 extension, ES6 normal-image transport and the precise ES5 square-root coefficient law.

stages.title: Discrete series: globalization, purity and Galois conjugation
stages.description: **Targets.** Fixed-ι tempered/discrete representations, Casselman’s criterion with central unitarity, the semisimple Gan–Harris–Sawin globalizations in no proper parabolic (Propositions 3.9/3.11, Appendix A), and arithmetic Weil–Deligne purity of weight 0 for semisimple discrete series (Theorem 1.2, Corollary 3.12). The general reductive adjoint statement is conditional on central reduction. Plan Galois conjugation for algebraic discrete-series models and embedding independence for geometric tempered representations. Trace-formula inputs, étale Kloosterman invariant vanishing, arbitrary discrete-series descent and reductive central reduction remain explicit gaps.

stages.title: The generic Ramanujan theorem
stages.description: **Targets.** Γ-stable test representations, parameter lifts through the actual central kernel over a finite extension, and the anchored weight argument. A fixed-ι tempered anchor gives fixed-ι integer weights; a discrete-series anchor supplies arithmetic integer weights at every embedding. The generic Ramanujan conclusion is planned with central compact factor at the generic place (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 5.4, pp.13–15, corrected scope). A nonsplit Frobenius component is not itself required to be central. Transfer on rational points to adjoint groups and spherical tempered-to-generic compatibility for general unramified quasi-split groups are requested at SR.4; arbitrary noncentral compact parts remain open.

stages.title: Elliptic parameters and the stack-purity route
stages.description: **Targets.** Ellipticity and weight-0 purity for semisimple global parameters. State Lafforgue–Zhu’s elliptic decomposition with invariants under the full centralizer S_σ, retaining the frozen leg and W^{G_m} in the GL_r example (Proposition 1.2, pp.2–3; Corollary 2.1, p.4). Define constant-coefficient stack realization (Ciubotaru–Harris Expectation 5.9, p.16). Its integer-weight consequence is conditional on DWP.8 stack integrality; deducing that realization from Satake-coefficient cohomology requires a separate bridge. Sun’s real ι-mixedness alone is not treated as that bridge or integer-weight theorem.

stages.title: Arthur homomorphism data and the discrete spectrum
stages.description: **Targets.** Weak global Arthur homomorphism data with continuous Weil factor and algebraic SL₂, and the separate conjectural arithmetic, Satake-compatibility and boundedness requirements (Ciubotaru–Harris Conjectures 1.3/1.8). Record the discrete-spectrum parametrization hypotheses (Conjectures 9.1/9.5), fixed-level rationality through the full Hecke algebra (Lemma 9.2, p.31), and Xue’s finite-codimension Hecke-quotient decomposition (Theorem 3.6.7, pp.30–31). Algebraicity requires a number-field model. Bare good-place compatibility has no ramified consequence; for Xue quotients use Li-Huerta Theorem 6.13, pp.47–48. No global Arthur homomorphism is constructed.

stages.title: Weight patterns, Property A and Arthur-type propagation
stages.description: **Targets.** Global weight patterns and propagation of complementary-series real parts, with the central-compact scope and ramified-anchor compatibility explicit (Ciubotaru–Harris Theorem 1.11, p.5). The symmetric weight array, Property A and Remark 10.8 (pp.33–35) compare boundary monodromy with good-place weights. Enumerated Sp6/F4/E7/E8 weight certificates eliminate extraneous points under the orbit-profile contracts; N3 must supply semantic orbit-to-triple identifications and the missing E7 profile. The endpoint (Theorem 10.3, pp.33–35) forces the central real part and vanishing on each global weight-graded monodromy piece, not vanishing of the full local discrete-series monodromy.
